risks.claim: NVIDIA's next reference architecture needs 100kW per rack
risks.assessment: The 100kW figure is widely cited in industry press but requires a primary public source (NVIDIA product page or published spec sheet). The H200 NVL in full node configuration is in the 60-80kW range per publicly available information. 100kW may apply to Vera Rubin or GB300 NVL configurations. Do not state a single number as definitive without citation.
risks.resolution: Change to a range framing: 'significantly exceeds legacy baselines, with current generation configurations requiring 60kW or more per rack depending on configuration'. Verify Vera Rubin and GB300 NVL specs when announced publicly.

risks.claim: Liquid cooling labor pool is approximately 1/100th the size of the air-cooling labor pool
risks.assessment: No public source supports this specific ratio. It is a rhetorical device in the source material, not a verifiable fact. If published as stated it would constitute a fabricated claim.
risks.resolution: Remove the ratio entirely. Replace with: 'Skilled liquid cooling commissioning and maintenance staff is a constrained workforce category. Workforce supply for liquid-cooled infrastructure has not scaled with deployment demand.' Cite a workforce or industry report if available.

risks.assessment: The $50/kWh figure appears to be a typo or unit error in the source notes (power is priced per kWh at a few cents to tens of cents typically; $50 would be extreme). If this refers to colocation power pricing in $/kW/month, the range is plausible for premium AI-ready sites but needs a public market source.
risks.resolution: Remove this figure entirely. Replace with a directional statement: 'AI-ready colo sites command significant premiums over legacy power contracts.' Verify against a public commercial real estate or colo pricing report before restating a number.

risks.claim: Most enterprise colo leases were signed at 8-15kW per rack
risks.assessment: Directionally consistent with industry baseline data. Uptime Institute and Omdia (formerly IHS Markit) have published data in this range. Not verifiable from a single freely accessible source in this pass.
risks.resolution: Frame as a directional claim with 'Needs verification' tag. Acceptable to state with 'historically' qualifier and note that recent AI-ready builds target significantly higher densities.

risks.claim: Air cooling caps out around 30kW per rack
risks.assessment: Industry consensus supports this directional claim. The specific threshold varies by facility and cooling design. Green Grid and ASHRAE have published guidance in this range but exact figures vary.
risks.resolution: State as 'practical ceiling in many facilities in the 25-40kW range' rather than a hard 30kW cutoff. Link to Green Grid or ASHRAE public guidance when finalizing.

risks.claim: EU enterprises placing orders in February already have their 2027 capacity; October orders get Q4 2027
risks.assessment: Reflects real supply chain dynamics but the specific month-to-delivery mapping is not verifiable from a public source. This reads like insider market knowledge rather than a public claim.
risks.resolution: Reframe as: 'Hardware lead times for AI-ready liquid-cooled infrastructure are extending. Enterprises evaluating 2027 capacity need to be making facility and hardware decisions now, not at year-end.' Remove the month-specific framing.

risks.claim: The 14kW-per-rack era ran from roughly 2010 to 2023
risks.assessment: Directionally accurate as a planning baseline. Safe to state as a general framing rather than a precise historical claim.
risks.resolution: Acceptable. State as 'legacy data center design standards common through the early 2020s'.

risks.claim: Microsoft transitions from air-cooled to chip-level liquid cooling
risks.assessment: Directly stated on Microsoft Learn public sustainability page. Verified.
